name: Clavicular's looksmaxxing philosophy

lead: Clavicular is the online alias of Braden Peters, an American streamer who became prominent in 2025 and 2026 on Kick and TikTok promoting extreme looksmaxxing. Wikipedia lists the practices he promotes as bonesmashing, anabolic steroids, methamphetamine for appetite suppression, and a paid course including guides on injectable peptides.
He is linked in media coverage to more extreme looksmaxxing and blackpill ideas. He denies that looksmaxxing is tied to incel culture.

paras: His approach is described as 'hardmaxxing': drug and injectable use, extreme dieting and physical modification, packaged as a paid course. Bonesmashing involves hitting facial bones to reshape the jaw and is described by medical sources as pseudoscientific.

Critics argue his content harms young men, and Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article says he overdosed on a livestream in 2026 after a five-drug 'pentastack'. Legal matters reported include arrests and charges, some dropped; a September 2026 Massachusetts charge is an allegation he denies.

lead: Clavicular is the online alias of Braden Eric Peters, an American influencer born in December 2005 and raised in Hoboken, New Jersey, who gained prominence through livestreams and clips on Kick and TikTok in 2025 and 2026 [1]. He promotes looksmaxxing, a trend of methods for improving appearance, and is associated with more extreme 'ascension' practices [1][2].

Practices Wikipedia attributes to his content include bonesmashing, anabolic steroids, methamphetamine used to suppress appetite, and a paid course originally called the Clavicular System, which includes guides on injectable peptides [1]. Medical sources describe bonesmashing as pseudoscientific [1]. Looksmaxxing's own critics, including doctors, call practices such as bonesmashing unsupported or dangerous [2].

His career has included controversy and legal events. These include a December 2025 livestream in which he drove a vehicle into a man, which he described as self-defence and after which Kick banned him, arrests in 2026 where charges were later dropped, and platform bans [1]. In September 2026 he was charged in Massachusetts with offences involving a 17-year-old; he has pleaded not guilty and denies the charges, and these remain allegations [1].

paras: He says he became interested in looksmaxxing in high school and spent much of the COVID-19 lockdowns online; he was expelled from Sacred Heart University after a short time there [1]. He has said he began testosterone injections at 14 and that he is autistic, though he has no professional diagnosis [1].

Wikipedia describes his content as promoting bonesmashing, steroids, methamphetamine for appetite suppression and peptide guides [1]. Wikipedia's looksmaxxing article says he is linked to promoting more extreme looksmaxxing and black pill ideology, and that in 2026 he overdosed on a livestream after taking a five-drug 'pentastack' previously revealed by Australian influencer Androgenic [2].

Wikipedia reports that he repeatedly used racial slurs on stream and has been accused of promoting misogyny and incel-linked ideas, which he denies; a 2025 video showed him injecting his then-17-year-old girlfriend with a fat-dissolving substance; and critics argue his content harms young men [1]. Events in 2026 included an Arizona arrest on drug and fake-ID charges later dropped, a Florida battery arrest, an alligator-related charge ended by plea deal and later dropped, and a permanent YouTube ban [1].
